speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis. The patient is a 53-year-old male who lost consciousness one hour ago immediately after micturating, found unconscious on the floor by his wife, and regained consciousness after approximately 30 seconds without confusion or amnesia. This classic presentation of transient loss of consciousness immediately following urination in a male suggests syncope due to mechanical stimulation of the vagus nerve (micturition syncope) or, more critically given the sudden onset and immediate recovery, a cardiac event triggered by the Valsalva maneuver or sudden movement. While micturition syncope is most likely, I must rule out other causes.
